options.summary: Also print N lines after each match
options.description: Print num lines of trailing context after each match. See also the -B and -C options.

options.summary: Treat all files as ASCII text.
options.description: Treat all files as ASCII text. Normally grep will simply print "Binary file... matches" if files contain binary characters. Use of this option forces grep to output lines matching the specified pattern.

options.summary: Also print N lines before each match
options.description: Print num lines of leading context before each match. See also the -A and -C options.

options.summary: The offset in bytes of a matched pattern is displayed in front of the respective matched line.
options.description: The offset in bytes of a matched pattern is displayed in front of the respective matched line.

options.summary: Print N lines of context on both sides of each match
options.description: Print num lines of leading and trailing context surrounding each match. See also the -A and -B options.

options.summary: Print how many lines matched instead of the lines
options.description: Only a count of selected lines is written to standard output.

options.summary: Highlight matches; WHEN is never, always or auto
options.description: Mark up the matching text with the expression stored in the GREP_COLOR environment variable. The possible values of when are "never", "always" and "auto".

examples.description: Print file name and line number for each match with color output

options.summary: Specify the demanded action for devices, FIFOs and sockets.
options.description: Specify the demanded action for devices, FIFOs and sockets. The default action is "read", which means, that they are read as if they were normal files. If the action is set to "skip", devices are silently skipped.

options.summary: Specify the demanded action for directories.
options.description: Specify the demanded action for directories. It is "read" by default, which means that the directories are read in the same manner as normal files. Other possible values are "skip" to silently ignore the directories, and "recurse" to read them recursively, which has the same effect as the -R and -r option.

options.summary: Use extended regular expressions, so | + ? ( ) need no backslash
options.description: Interpret pattern as an extended regular expression (i.e., force grep to behave as egrep).

examples.description: Use extended `regex`es (supports `?`, `+`, `{}`, `()`, and `|`), in case-insensitive mode

options.summary: Give a pattern explicitly; repeat for several, or use for patterns starting with -
options.description: Specify a pattern used during the search of the input: an input line is selected if it matches any of the specified patterns. This option is most useful when multiple -e options are used to specify multiple patterns, or when a pattern begins with a dash ('-').

options.summary: If specified, it excludes files matching the given filename pattern from the search.
options.description: If specified, it excludes files matching the given filename pattern from the search. Note that --exclude and --include patterns are processed in the order given. If a name matches multiple patterns, the latest matching rule wins. If no --include pattern is specified, all files are searched that are not excluded. Patterns are matched to the full path specified, not only to the filename component.

options.summary: If -R is specified, it excludes directories matching the given filename pattern from the search.
options.description: If -R is specified, it excludes directories matching the given filename pattern from the search. Note that --exclude-dir and --include-dir patterns are processed in the order given. If a name matches multiple patterns, the latest matching rule wins. If no --include-dir pattern is specified, all directories are searched that are not excluded.

options.summary: Treat the pattern as a literal string, not a regex
options.description: Interpret pattern as a set of fixed strings (i.e., force grep to behave as fgrep).

options.summary: Read one or more newline separated patterns from file.
options.description: Read one or more newline separated patterns from file. Empty pattern lines match every input line. Newlines are not considered part of a pattern. If file is empty, nothing is matched.

options.summary: Interpret pattern as a basic regular expression (i.e., force grep to behave as traditional grep).
options.description: Interpret pattern as a basic regular expression (i.e., force grep to behave as traditional grep).

options.summary: Prefix each match with its file name
options.description: Always print filename headers with output lines.

examples.description: Print file name and line number for each match with color output

options.summary: Never print filename headers (i.e., filenames) with output lines.
options.description: Never print filename headers (i.e., filenames) with output lines.

options.summary: Print a brief help message.
options.description: Print a brief help message.

options.summary: Skip binary files
options.description: Ignore binary files. This option is equivalent to the "--binary-files=without-match" option.

examples.description: Search for a pattern in all files recursively in a directory, ignoring binary files

options.summary: Match regardless of upper or lower case
options.description: Perform case insensitive matching. By default, grep is case sensitive.

examples.description: Use extended `regex`es (supports `?`, `+`, `{}`, `()`, and `|`), in case-insensitive mode

options.summary: If specified, only files matching the given filename pattern are searched.
options.description: If specified, only files matching the given filename pattern are searched. Note that --include and --exclude patterns are processed in the order given. If a name matches multiple patterns, the latest matching rule wins. Patterns are matched to the full path specified, not only to the filename component.

options.summary: If -R is specified, only directories matching the given filename pattern are searched.
options.description: If -R is specified, only directories matching the given filename pattern are searched. Note that --include-dir and --exclude-dir patterns are processed in the order given. If a name matches multiple patterns, the latest matching rule wins.

options.summary: Only the names of files not containing selected lines are written to standard output.
options.description: Only the names of files not containing selected lines are written to standard output. Pathnames are listed once per file searched. If the standard input is searched, the string "(standard input)" is written unless a --label is specified.

options.summary: List only the names of files that contain a match
options.description: Only the names of files containing selected lines are written to standard output. grep will only search a file until a match has been found, making searches potentially less expensive. Pathnames are listed once per file searched. If the standard input is searched, the string "(standard input)" is written unless a --label is specified.

options.summary: Label to use in place of "(standard input)" for a file name where a file name would normally be printed.
options.description: Label to use in place of "(standard input)" for a file name where a file name would normally be printed. This option applies to -H, -L, and -l.

options.summary: Use mmap(2) instead of read(2) to read input, which can result in better performance under some circumstances but can cause undefined behaviour.
options.description: Use mmap(2) instead of read(2) to read input, which can result in better performance under some circumstances but can cause undefined behaviour.

options.summary: Stop reading the file after num matches.
options.description: Stop reading the file after num matches.

options.summary: Show where each match is, as a line number before it
options.description: Each output line is preceded by its relative line number in the file, starting at line 1. The line number counter is reset for each file processed. This option is ignored if -c, -L, -l, or -q is specified.

examples.description: Print file name and line number for each match with color output

options.summary: Prints a zero-byte after the file name.
options.description: Prints a zero-byte after the file name.

options.summary: If -R is specified, follow symbolic links only if they were explicitly listed on the command line.
options.description: If -R is specified, follow symbolic links only if they were explicitly listed on the command line. The default is not to follow symbolic links.

options.summary: Print just the matched text, one match per line
options.description: Prints only the matching part of the lines.

options.summary: If -R is specified, no symbolic links are followed.
options.description: If -R is specified, no symbolic links are followed. This is the default.

options.summary: Print nothing; only set the exit status (0 if anything matched)
options.description: Quiet mode: suppress normal output. grep will only search a file until a match has been found, making searches potentially less expensive.

options.summary: Search directories recursively
options.description: Recursively search subdirectories listed. (i.e., force grep to behave as rgrep).

examples.description: Search for a pattern in all files recursively in a directory, ignoring binary files

options.summary: If -R is specified, all symbolic links are followed.
options.description: If -R is specified, all symbolic links are followed. The default is not to follow symbolic links.

options.summary: Silent mode.
options.description: Silent mode. Nonexistent and unreadable files are ignored (i.e., their error messages are suppressed).

options.summary: Search binary files, but do not attempt to print them.
options.description: Search binary files, but do not attempt to print them.

options.summary: This option has no effect and is provided only for compatibility with GNU grep.
options.description: This option has no effect and is provided only for compatibility with GNU grep.

options.summary: Display version information and exit.
options.description: Display version information and exit.

options.summary: Show the lines that do NOT match
options.description: Selected lines are those not matching any of the specified patterns.

examples.description: Read data from `stdin` and do not print lines that match a pattern

options.summary: Only match whole words
options.description: The expression is searched for as a word (as if surrounded by '[[:<:]]' and '[[:>:]]'; see re_format(7)). This option has no effect if -x is also specified.

options.summary: Only input lines selected against an entire fixed string or regular expression are considered to be matching lines.
options.description: Only input lines selected against an entire fixed string or regular expression are considered to be matching lines.

options.summary: Equivalent to -i.
options.description: Equivalent to -i. Obsoleted.

options.summary: Treat input and output data as sequences of lines terminated by a zero-byte instead of a newline.
options.description: Treat input and output data as sequences of lines terminated by a zero-byte instead of a newline.

options.summary: Controls searching and printing of binary files.
options.description:
Controls searching and printing of binary files. Options are:

binary (default)
Search binary files but do not print them.

without-match
Do not search binary files.

text
Treat all files as text.

options.summary: Force output to be line buffered.
options.description: Force output to be line buffered. By default, output is line buffered when standard output is a terminal and block buffered otherwise.
